323761207.body:
First public release of the HyperOS/MIUI14+ bootloader unlock method, reverse-engineered from the Little Kernel bootloader and proven with RPMB dumps.

## The problem this solves

Since MIUI 14.0.3 and HyperOS, `mtkclient da seccfg unlock` reports success but the bootloader remains locked after reboot. This bug has been open in mtkclient for 2+ years across multiple Xiaomi MediaTek devices ([#81](https://github.com/bkerler/mtkclient/issues/81), [#764](https://github.com/bkerler/mtkclient/issues/764), [#1219](https://github.com/bkerler/mtkclient/issues/1219), [#1405](https://github.com/bkerler/mtkclient/issues/1405)).

**Root cause:** Xiaomi added a second lock layer in RPMB that overrides seccfg.
**The fix:** erase the RPMB magic — the LK then falls back to seccfg, which mtkclient can write to UNLOCK.

## What's in this release

- **Full technical writeup** (`README.md`) — root cause analysis, dual-layer lock mechanism, the 3-command unlock method
- **Ghidra decompilation proof** (`proof/VERIFICATION.md`) — decompiled `mi_check_magic` function, RPMB before/after dumps with SHA256, mtkclient source audit
- **`scan_lk.py`** — LK binary compatibility scanner with 0-100% verdict scoring
- **Device compatibility database** (`COMPATIBILITY.md`) — Tier 1-4 device classification
- **GitHub issue template** for structured community device reports
- AGPL-3.0 license

## Tested on

| Device | Codename | SoC | Firmware | Result |
|--------|----------|-----|----------|--------|
| POCO M4 Pro 4G | fleur | MT6781 | HyperOS OS1.0.11.0.TKEEUXM | Unlocked, persistent |

## Quick start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Jz8Root/xiaomi-hyperos-bootloader-unlock
cd xiaomi-hyperos-bootloader-unlock

# Scan your LK binary first
python3 scan_lk.py /path/to/lk_a.img

# Then follow README.md → "The Method — 3 Commands"
```

## Warnings

- Backup RPMB and NV partitions before anything
- This wipes your data (factory reset on first boot after unlock)
- BROM V6 (MT6789+) is patched in hardware — this method won't work
- Only HyperOS 1 has been verified — HyperOS 2/3 untested
- Voids manufacturer warranty

## Help wanted

If you successfully unlock another device, please file a [Device Test Report](https://github.com/Jz8Root/xiaomi-hyperos-bootloader-unlock/issues/new?template=device-report.yml). Each successful report expands the compatibility database for everyone.

## Links

- [XDA thread](https://xdaforums.com/t/4784527/)
- [mtkclient](https://github.com/bkerler/mtkclient) — the foundation

## Credits

- [bkerler/mtkclient](https://github.com/bkerler/mtkclient) — Xiaomi MTK BROM + DA framework
- The Kamakiri exploit researchers
- Everyone who reported the seccfg bug on GitHub — your reports helped map the scope

---
Researched & tested by **Jz8root**.

342854090.body:
Community expansion release: 6 hardware unlocks confirmed across 4 SoCs, covering the full HyperOS lifecycle (1, 2, 3). New SoC-specific RPMB sector discovery, A/B slot divergence after OTA documented, and community-contributed improvements.

## What's new since v1.0.0

- **5 new Tier 1 devices** proven on hardware by community testers
- **RPMB sector is SoC-specific** — MT6781/MT6769Z = 57344, MT6833 = 65504. Always grep before erasing. (Discovered by KTS618)
- **lk_a ≠ lk_b after OTA** — slot A and slot B can carry different LK builds. Always scan both. (Discovered by piotrurban)
- **HyperOS 1 + 2 + 3 confirmed** — the RPMB lock mechanism is consistent across all HyperOS generations
- **Step 0 added** — mandatory sector discovery via `grep -boa "Jz8PNRUF" rpmb_dump.bin`
- **Linux pre-flight documented** — ModemManager kill + kernel module unload (PR #6 by miromraz)
- **scan_lk.py as decision gate** — README restructured to route users through the scanner first (PR #5 by miromraz)
- **Windows struct.error FAQ** — documented USB bulk driver limitation + WSL2 / Live USB workaround
- **Boot flow diagram** — mi_check_magic() decision tree added to README

## Tested on

| Device | Codename | SoC | Firmware | RPMB Sector | Result | Tester |
|--------|----------|-----|----------|-------------|--------|--------|
| POCO M4 Pro 4G | fleur | MT6781 | HyperOS 1.0.11.0 | 57344 | Unlocked, persistent | Jz8root |
| Redmi Note 11 4G | fleur (2201117SY) | MT6781 | HyperOS 1.0 | — | Unlocked (Path B, seccfg only) | miromraz |
| Redmi Note 11S Global | miel | MT6781 | HyperOS 1.0.9.0 | 57344 | Unlocked, persistent | ITSME |
| Redmi Note 11S | miel | MT6781 | HyperOS 1.0.9.0 | 57344 | Unlocked, persistent | kwhj4ff67r-crypto |
| Redmi Note 13 5G | gold | MT6833 | HyperOS 3.0.9.0 / Android 15 | **65504** | Unlocked, persistent | KTS618 |
| Redmi 12 | fire | MT6769Z | HyperOS 2.0.207 | 57344 | Unlocked, persistent | piotrurban |

## Quick start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Jz8Root/xiaomi-hyperos-bootloader-unlock
cd xiaomi-hyperos-bootloader-unlock

# Step 0: Scan your LK binary (scan BOTH slots)
python3 scan_lk.py /path/to/lk_a.bin
python3 scan_lk.py /path/to/lk_b.bin

# Step 0b: Find your RPMB sector (do NOT skip)
python3 mtk.py da rpmb r rpmb_dump.bin
grep -boa "Jz8PNRUF" rpmb_dump.bin
# sector = byte_offset / 256

# Then follow README.md → "The Method — 3 Commands"
```

## Warnings

- Backup RPMB and NV partitions before anything
- This wipes your data (factory reset on first boot after unlock)
- BROM V6 (MT6789+) is patched in hardware — this method won't work
- **RPMB sector is NOT universal** — always grep the dump first. Sector 57344 is only confirmed for MT6781/MT6769Z. MT6833 uses 65504.
- **Scan both LK slots** — after an OTA, lk_a and lk_b can diverge
- **Use Linux** for the RPMB erase step — Windows USB drivers cause struct.error
- Voids manufacturer warranty

## Help wanted

If you successfully unlock another device, please file a [Device Test Report](https://github.com/Jz8Root/xiaomi-hyperos-bootloader-unlock/issues/new/choose). Each successful report expands the compatibility database for everyone.

**Priority targets:** Redmi 9A/9C (MT6762), Redmi 12C (MT6765/MT6769) — issue [#81](https://github.com/bkerler/mtkclient/issues/81) has been waiting since 2021.

## Links

- [XDA thread](https://xdaforums.com/t/4784527/)
- [mtkclient](https://github.com/bkerler/mtkclient) — the foundation

## Credits

- **bkerler/mtkclient** — Xiaomi MTK BROM + DA framework
- The Kamakiri exploit researchers
- **miromraz** — PR #5 (README restructure), PR #6 (Linux pre-flight), Path B confirmation, SK Hynix RPMB layout
- **KTS618** — MT6833 sector 65504 discovery, first HyperOS 3.0 confirmation
- **piotrurban** — lk_a/lk_b OTA divergence discovery, first HyperOS 2.0 confirmation
- **ITSME** — first independent hardware confirmation (miel)
- **kwhj4ff67r-crypto** — miel replication
- Everyone who reported the seccfg bug on GitHub — your reports helped map the scope

*Researched by Jz8root. Community tested.*

426753831.body:
# v2.1.0 — Evidence-driven scanner, Tier 3b mapping, 10 hardware confirmations

This release changes the project from a largely SoC-guided recipe into an
evidence-driven workflow: scan both LK slots, inspect the live RPMB state, use
the measured sector, and treat contradictory signals as an investigation rather
than guessing a destructive path.

Since v2.0.0, the repository has accumulated 22 commits, new hardware families,
two hard-block clusters, upstream mtkclient work and the first scanner regression
suite.

## Scanner Safety Gates

`scan_lk.py` now distinguishes binary capability from live device state.

- `COMPATIBLE_FULL` requires both the known `Jz8PNRUF` mechanism and detected
  seccfg support.
- A magic-absent LK that still exposes exact `mi_get_lock_state` now returns
  `MAYBE` instead of a false `COMPATIBLE_SECCFG_ONLY`. Issue
  [#10](https://github.com/Jz8Root/xiaomi-hyperos-bootloader-unlock/issues/10)
  supplied the real counterexample.
- `COMPATIBLE_SECCFG_ONLY` is now explicitly a clean Path B candidate, not proof
  that every magic-absent build will unlock.
- RPMB size constants remain informational and carry no score because they occur
  naturally in unrelated binaries.
- `COMPATIBLE_FULL` no longer claims the live RPMB record is initialized merely
  because the LK contains the code.

Five regression tests cover full Path A, clean Path B, contradictory RPMB
signals, missing seccfg and preloader-like input.

## Important Upgrade Note

Do not reuse a v2.0.0 scanner verdict without rescanning.

1. Dump and scan both `lk_a` and `lk_b`.
2. Use the result for the active slot.
3. For Path A, dump RPMB and locate `Jz8PNRUF`; never select a sector from the
   SoC name alone.
4. Treat `MAYBE` and `UNKNOWN` as stop conditions requiring manual analysis.
5. Remember that the Path B score tops out at 44/100 by construction; it is not
   a confidence percentage.

## New Hardware Evidence

The project now records 10 hardware unlock reports across HyperOS 1, 2 and 3 on
three confirmed SoC families.

- POCO M4 5G `thunder` / MT6833 `light` was unlocked persistently by
  [@ogmkp](https://github.com/ogmkp) in
  [#18](https://github.com/Jz8Root/xiaomi-hyperos-bootloader-unlock/issues/18).
- POCO M4 Pro 4G `fleur` / MT6781 received another independent persistent
  confirmation from staxifrage in
  [#19](https://github.com/Jz8Root/xiaomi-hyperos-bootloader-unlock/issues/19).
- Redmi Note 13 5G `gold` / MT6833 received a second independent confirmation
  from Gkhupo in
  [#17](https://github.com/Jz8Root/xiaomi-hyperos-bootloader-unlock/issues/17).

Issue #19 also confirmed slot-asymmetric LK generations on `fleur`: `lk_a` was a
Path B candidate while active `lk_b` was Path A. This independently reproduces
the earlier `fire` A/B divergence and makes scanning both slots mandatory.

## MT6833 Is Driver-Family-Specific

MT6833 no longer has one universal sector:

| LK family | Device family | Measured sector | Dump offset |
|-|-|-|-|
| `gold` | Dimensity 6080 | 65504 | `0xFFE000` |
| `light` | Dimensity 700 | 57344 | `0xE00000` |

The `light` LK truncates the selected internal address with `uxth`, reducing its
base candidates to `0xE000`. This is measured hardware behavior, not a
storage-vendor guess.

## Tier 3b: Writes Persist, Boot Restores The Magic

MT6877 (`rubypro` and `pissarro`) and Redmi 12C `earth` form two measured
hard-block clusters for the RPMB method. A matching `pissarropro` failure was
reported separately, but without the same public dump-level trace.

- The erase reaches flash and survives a cold BROM re-entry.
- seccfg can persist as state 3.
- A normal boot path restores exactly the eight `Jz8PNRUF` bytes.
- Fastboot therefore remains locked.

vivaad's cold-cycle experiment in
[#8](https://github.com/Jz8Root/xiaomi-hyperos-bootloader-unlock/issues/8)
proves restoration occurs during the normal boot chain, but does not isolate the
exact writer. Documentation now says `early boot chain`, not `preloader`, until
a call trace or instrumented stage identifies it.

## MT6893 Reclassified

The Xiaomi 11T `agate` logs in
[#14](https://github.com/Jz8Root/xiaomi-hyperos-bootloader-unlock/issues/14)
prove Kamakiri runs on MT6893. The SoC has been removed from the old numeric
Tier 4 inference.

The unlock path remains unresolved:

- MIUI 12.5 persisted seccfg state 3 but remained locked with no live RPMB magic.
- A supplied HyperOS 1.0.15 LK scans `COMPATIBLE_FULL` and contains the explicit
  string `1st time run MI Lock, write magic`.
- Active slot, second LK slot and live HyperOS RPMB state are still pending.

## mtkclient Contributions

- [mtkclient #307](https://github.com/bkerler/mtkclient/pull/307), already
  merged, prevents RPMB result codes from being silently discarded.
- [mtkclient #426](https://github.com/bkerler/mtkclient/pull/426) proposes a
  generic fix for the optional Thumb NOP that shifted the MT6833 UFS HBA literal.
- [mtkclient #427](https://github.com/bkerler/mtkclient/pull/427) proposes
  restoring MEID correctly from saved JSON DA state.

PRs #426 and #427 are open and passing CI at release time; they are not described
as merged.

## Documentation And Procedure Corrections

- Sector selection is dump-driven and indexed by LK/storage-driver family.
- Hits exactly 16 MiB apart are documented as 16-bit RPMB address aliases, not
  independent copies.
- USB 3.x write failures and Tier 3b boot restoration are treated as separate
  failure modes.
- `fastboot getvar unlocked` remains authoritative; `oem lks` is optional.
- Userdata/metadata wipe guidance is conditional. Assume data loss, but issue
  #18 proves an explicit wipe is not universal.
- Dead legacy issue links and unsupported device/SoC pairings were removed.
- Device reports now request storage identifiers and active-slot/LK-build data.

## Known Limitations

- No verified RPMB-method bypass exists yet for the Tier 3b restoration clusters.
- The exact early-boot writer restoring `Jz8PNRUF` is not identified.
- Issue #10 still needs its RPMB dump and current fastboot identity.
- Issue #14 still needs `lk_b`, active-slot and live RPMB data.
- Issue #19 still needs exact LK build strings and hashes.
- The alternative LK-public-key/token-forging approach linked in issue #13 has
  no public persistent-unlock proof for rubypro yet.

## Credits

Hardware evidence and corrections in this cycle came from ogmkp, staxifrage,
vivaad, LucaCraft89, burg1ar, Gkhupo, katavnnn, miromraz, piotrurban and the
other testers who preserved logs, hashes and negative results instead of only
reporting success or failure.

Full comparison:
https://github.com/Jz8Root/xiaomi-hyperos-bootloader-unlock/compare/v2.0.0...v2.1.0
